title: formula: a CEL parse refusal keeps the parser's error kind and position, so editors can say what is wrong and where in plain words (#27837)
body:
domain:ui#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaJoinvGQSbHeDaWBe

Filing gate: ③ triage-directed. #27521 row 36 (carded as #27837) asked for parser errors in plain words. PR #27901 does what the ui can with what it is given and names this producer seam in its report (6513955821, `out_of_scope_findings`, class b).
Reach: every CEL editor in Studio and Setup (formula fields, validation conditions, flow expressions) that shows a syntax error.
Reader who acts: `domain:engine` (`packages/formula`).
Duplicate search: `search_issues` "@objectstack/formula invalid-cel refusal parse error code range position" and "formula package cel parse error position" → no open card covering it (#4812 is closed and about lint bypassing the parser).

## Observed
`@objectstack/formula` folds every cel-js parse error into one refusal code, `invalid-cel`, carrying only the engine's detail text (e.g. "Unexpected token: EOF … ^"). The `ParseError`'s own code and range are dropped, and the `pos` that `EvalError` declares is never filled. So an editor can show only one generic plain sentence above the raw detail (what PR #27901 does), and cannot say "a closing bracket is missing at character 14".

## Wanted
The refusal keeps the parser's error kind (e.g. unexpected end, unexpected token, unknown function) and its position (offset or range) as structured fields beside the existing `message`, with the message unchanged so current readers are not affected. Fill `EvalError.pos` where the evaluator knows it. Editors can then map each kind to a plain sentence and point to the position.

Related: #27837, PR #27901, #27521 (row 36).
